key_claims: The UN Monitoring Team assesses that Taliban and al-Qaeda remain closely aligned with no sign of a break, cemented by marriage and second-generation ties.

Member states estimate the Taliban contest or control 50-70% of Afghan territory outside urban centers and directly control 57% of district centers, with emphasis on contesting rather than holding ground.
One member state assessed Sirajuddin Haqqani as part of wider al-Qaeda leadership (the 'Ateen' Shura), a point left in a footnote.
Taliban claim to have zero foreign fighters, yet the report documents over 10,000 foreign fighters including TTP, IMU and TIP.
ISKP leader Shahab al-Muhajir coordinates with the al-Siddiq office, part of ISIS's new regional hubs-and-spokes structure for Central and South Asia.
Member states disagree on whether Haqqani Network and ISKP collude; fluid personnel movement and shared interests in undermining Kabul are noted.
Roughly 85% of targeted assassinations in Afghanistan are attributed by member states to the Taliban, who leave them unclaimed.
Al-Qaeda faces a succession issue due to Zawahiri's probable poor health.
